record.original_question: Let MUB(d) denote the maximum number of pairwise mutually unbiased orthonormal bases in C^d. Is it true that in dimension 6 one cannot have a complete set of seven such bases, i.e. does MUB(6) < 7 hold?

evidence.quote: For d not a prime power, the problem of determining MUB(d) is still open. The smallest open instance is particularly well known for being a tantalizing open problem ... Conjecture 22. Let MUB(d) denote the largest possible number of (simultaneously) mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) in C^d. We have MUB(6) < 7.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $d\ge 2$, two orthonormal bases $\{e_1,\dots,e_d\}$ and $\{f_1,\dots,f_d\}$ of the Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^d$ (with the standard Hermitian inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$) are called mutually unbiased if
\[ |\langle e_i, f_j\rangle|^2 \;=\; \frac{1}{d} \qquad \text{for all } i,j\in\{1,\dots,d\}. \]
A family $\mathcal{B}_1,\dots,\mathcal{B}_N$ of orthonormal bases of $\mathbb{C}^d$ is called a set of mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) if every pair $\mathcal{B}_a,\mathcal{B}_b$ with $a\ne b$ is mutually unbiased. Define
\[ \mathrm{MUB}(d) \;=\; \max\{\, N : \text{there exist } N \text{ pairwise mutually unbiased orthonormal bases of } \mathbb{C}^d\,\}. \]
It is known that $\mathrm{MUB}(d) \le d+1$ for every $d$, with equality when $d$ is a prime power, and that $\mathrm{MUB}(6)\ge 3$.

Prove or disprove: $\mathrm{MUB}(6) < 7$, i.e. there is no complete set of seven mutually unbiased bases in $\mathbb{C}^6$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether $\mathrm{MUB}(6)=7$ (or even whether four MUBs exist in dimension 6) is a well-known long-standing open problem. As of 2025 it remains unresolved; recent work (e.g. a 2025 Phys. Rev. A paper formulating MUB existence as a polynomial optimization problem) provides new algorithmic frameworks but does not settle the question, and no proof of $\mathrm{MUB}(6)<7$ has appeared.

status_evidence.title: Mutually unbiased bases - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In the smallest composite dimension, six, it is known that between three and seven mutually unbiased bases exist... a decades-old conjecture (Zauner's) states that there exist at most three.
status_evidence.claim: MUB(6) is not known; a complete set of 7 is conjectured not to exist.

status_evidence.title: Mutually unbiased bases as a commuting polynomial optimization problem, Phys. Rev. A (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Formulates the MUB existence problem as polynomial optimization; algorithm would eventually settle dimension six but remains intractable in practice.

status_evidence.title: Randomstrasse 101 — MUBs, ETFs, and Zauner's Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Lists MUB(6)<7 as an open conjecture.
